name: California
rateNote: County auctions property — 1-year challenge period after sale
auctionPlatform: GovEase (LA County and most major counties)
auctionTiming: Year-round — LA County 2026 confirmed April and June via GovEase
keyNotes: 1-year challenge period after sale — title companies will not insure during this window
IRS liens survive tax deed sale — always check federal liens before bidding
LA County 2026 auctions: April and June confirmed on GovEase
High competition in coastal counties — best value in Central Valley and inland
summary: California requires minimum 5 years of tax delinquency before county auctions. Opening bids are set near assessed value. Conducted by county tax collectors. Statute: CA Rev & Tax Code §3691.
typeWhy: California sells the property deed outright at auction after 5 years of tax delinquency. There is no post-sale redemption period — the buyer receives full title. CA Rev & Tax Code §3691.
rateWhy: California uses market-value bidding at auction with opening bids set near assessed value. There is no statutory interest rate because the state sells the deed outright. CA Rev & Tax Code §3691.
notBeginnerReason: Minimum 5 years delinquency, bids open at market value, intense institutional competition, no direct purchase.
beginnerTip: California is not a beginner state. If you're set on California, look at rural counties (Lassen, Modoc, Siskiyou) where competition is lower and opening bids are lower.
risks: Opening bids near market value — little to no discount
Institutional competition is among the highest in the country
5-year delinquency requirement creates very limited inventory
Tenants have strong protections — factor eviction costs into any occupied property
ddExtra: Verify 5-year delinquency is fully met before bidding
Check for active tenants — California eviction process can take 12–18 months
Run title search for IRS liens, HOA super-liens, and Mello-Roos assessments

steps: Find your target county's tax sale schedule at the county tax collector's website
Register on Bid4Assets.com or the county's auction platform
Submit a deposit (typically $500–$5,000 depending on county) to qualify for bidding
Bid online or in person per county instructions — opening bids are near market value

rules.administrator: Each of 58 counties — County Tax Collector (or Treasurer-Tax Collector)
rules.stateOversight: CA State Controller's Office provides guidance and oversight — sco.ca.gov/ardtax_public_auction.html
rules.critical: ⚡ California does NOT sell tax lien certificates. Properties sold outright at auction. No redemption after auction starts.

process.step1: Property taxes unpaid → declared tax-defaulted at 12:01 AM July 1 of that fiscal year (RTC §3436)
process.step2: Tax collector records Notice of Power to Sell in county recorder's office after 5-year threshold (3yr for nonresidential commercial/vacant)
process.step3: Board of Supervisors approves sale by resolution (RTC §3694). Property listed for auction.
process.step4: Notice published in local newspaper 3 times in successive 7-day intervals before sale date (RTC §3702)
process.step5: Certified mail notice sent 45–120 days before sale to all parties of interest (owners, lienholders) per RTC §3701
process.step6: Public auction — online (GovEase or Bid4Assets) or in-person. Sold to highest bidder above minimum.
process.step7: Right to redeem ceases at 5:00 PM LAST BUSINESS DAY before auction date. Redemption impossible after.
process.step8: Winning bidder pays full purchase price. Tax Collector's Deed issued and recorded.
process.step9: Current-year taxes (not yet delinquent at time of sale) are NOT in minimum bid — buyer must pay separately.

defaultThresholds.residential: 5 years from date taxes first became tax-defaulted
defaultThresholds.publicBenefit: 3 years (public agency or nonprofit acquiring for public benefit per §3692.4)
defaultThresholds.note: Installment Plan (5-pay) MUST be initiated BEFORE property reaches power-to-sell status. Cannot start after 5-year threshold.

installmentPlan.name: Installment Plan of Redemption (5-Year Payment Plan)
installmentPlan.eligibility: Only available BEFORE property reaches power-to-sell (i.e., within first 5 years of default for residential)
installmentPlan.terms: 20% down payment of total defaulted amount. Remaining balance in 4 annual installments.
installmentPlan.default: If plan defaults — new plan cannot be initiated until July 1 of following fiscal year
installmentPlan.note: ⚡ Once property is 5+ years tax-defaulted (Subject to Power to Sell) — installment plan CLOSED. Must pay in full or face auction.

auction.frequency: As scheduled by each county — typically annually. Some counties: multiple auctions per year.
auction.platforms: GovEase (Los Angeles, Humboldt, San Bernardino, and others) + Bid4Assets (Butte, Monterey, Riverside, Siskiyou, San Diego, and others) + some counties in-person
auction.bidMethod: Premium bid — highest bidder above minimum bid
auction.minimumBid: County-set — typically all defaulted taxes + penalties + interest + costs of sale. Some counties: minimum may also include assessed value floor.
auction.registration: Advance registration required. Deposit required before bidding (typically $2,500–$5,000 depending on county).
auction.payment: Full purchase price due within time specified by tax collector (typically within 3–5 business days post-auction)
auction.currentYearTaxes: ⚡ Current year secured taxes NOT included in minimum bid. Buyer responsible for paying separately when they become due.
auction.defaultBidder: Bidder who fails to consummate sale forfeits deposit. Tax collector may ban bidder from sales for up to 5 years (RTC §3698.5(e)).
auction.ownerBidding: Current owner may NOT purchase own property at auction below minimum bid (RTC §3698.5(d))

otc.name: Unsold / Re-offer Properties
otc.process: If property offered at auction and no acceptable bid received — tax collector may offer same property at reduced minimum within 90 days. Repeatedly unsold properties re-offered at intervals of ≤6 years until sold.
otc.note: Contact county tax collector for unsold property lists. No statewide OTC platform — county by county.

subTax.name: N/A — California deed state. No lien cert mechanism.

redemption.preAuction: Owner (or parties of interest) may redeem (pay ALL defaulted taxes + penalties + interest + costs) at any time until 5:00 PM on last business day before auction date
redemption.postAuction: ⚡ ZERO right of redemption after auction. No exceptions.
redemption.note: ⚡ IRS federal tax lien: 120-day redemption right from sale date if IRS lien recorded against property

deedPath.name: Tax Collector's Deed
deedPath.effect: Conveys title FREE AND CLEAR of most encumbrances existing before sale (RTC §3712)
exceptions: Installments of taxes/special assessments becoming payable on secured roll AFTER sale date (buyer pays going forward)
Liens of any taxing agency that does NOT consent to the sale under Ch.7
Special assessment liens not included in redemption amount (where non-consenting agency involved)
⚡ IRS federal tax liens: 120-day post-sale redemption right for IRS
Easements and rights-of-way of record NOT extinguished
deedPath.prop13: ⚡ Prop 13 reassessment: property reassessed at purchase price as new base year value. Buyer's property taxes going forward based on purchase price.
deedPath.titleInsurance: ⚡ CRITICAL: 1-year challenge period after deed recorded (RTC §3725, §177). Title companies typically will NOT issue title insurance during this period UNLESS: quiet title action successfully completed OR quitclaim deeds obtained from former assessee AND all lienholders.
deedPath.challengePeriod: 1 year from deed recordation — former assessee or lienholder may challenge validity of sale

excessProceeds.name: Excess Proceeds
excessProceeds.definition: Any amount exceeding $150 remaining after satisfying: taxes, assessment liens, and costs of sale
excessProceeds.claimWindow: 1 year from date Tax Collector's deed to purchaser is RECORDED
excessProceeds.priority: 1st: Lienholders of record (by priority of lien). 2nd: Former owner(s) with title of record at time of sale.
excessProceeds.afterExpiry: Unclaimed excess after 1 year → transferred to county general fund
excessProceeds.assignment: ⚡ Right to claim excess proceeds can ONLY be assigned through dated written instrument that explicitly states the assignment AND states each party has informed the other of the VALUE of the right being assigned. (Protects former owners from predatory excess proceeds buyers.)
excessProceeds.process: File claim form with county within 1 year of deed recordation. County board of supervisors (or delegated officer, typically treasurer-tax collector) reviews claims.
excessProceeds.challenge: 90-day window to challenge county's determination on excess proceeds claim
excessProceeds.scoGuide: State Controller's Office Excess Proceeds Guide: sco.ca.gov/Files-ARD-Tax-Info/Tax-Collector-Ref-Man/SCO_ExcessProceedsGuide.pdf

es.summary: California requiere mínimo 5 años de morosidad. Las pujas iniciales se establecen cerca del valor tasado. Estatuto: CA Rev & Tax Code §3691.
es.typeWhy: California es un estado de escritura porque el recaudador del condado vende la propiedad directamente al postor ganador sin derecho de redención posterior a la venta (CA Rev & Tax Code §3691).
es.rateWhy: No existe una tasa de interés fija porque las pujas se abren cerca del valor tasado de la propiedad. El retorno del inversor depende exclusivamente del diferencial entre el precio de compra y el valor de mercado.
es.notBeginnerReason: Mínimo 5 años de morosidad, pujas a valor de mercado, intensa competencia institucional, sin compra directa.
es.beginnerTip: California no es un estado para principiantes. Si insiste, mire condados rurales (Lassen, Modoc, Siskiyou) donde la competencia y las pujas son más bajas.
risks: Pujas iniciales cerca del valor de mercado — poco o ningún descuento
Competencia institucional entre las más altas del país
Requisito de 5 años crea inventario muy limitado
Inquilinos con fuertes protecciones — desalojo puede tomar 12–18 meses
ddExtra: Verifique que se cumplieron los 5 años de morosidad antes de pujar
Revise inquilinos activos — proceso de desalojo de CA puede tomar 12–18 meses
Ejecute búsqueda de título para gravámenes IRS, super-gravámenes HOA y evaluaciones Mello-Roos

auctionSignup.platform: Bid4Assets.com (mayoría de condados) o portales específicos del condado
steps: Encuentre el calendario de venta fiscal de su condado en el sitio del recaudador
Regístrese en Bid4Assets.com o en la plataforma del condado
Envíe un depósito ($500–$5,000 según el condado) para calificar
Puje en línea o en persona — las pujas iniciales son cerca del valor de mercado
auctionSignup.depositInfo: Depósito requerido. Varía por condado — normalmente $500–$5,000.
